articlesShipped.title: How to Prune a Monterey Cypress Hedge in Broadstairs: Timing, the No-Brown-Wood Rule and Canker Watch for CT10
articlesShipped.category: Coastal species choice and salt-wind resilience
articlesShipped.sourceChannel: Royal Horticultural Society (rhs.org.uk/plants/leylandii/pruning-guide, applicable to Cupressus macrocarpa per the RHS guide itself; rhs.org.uk plant profiles for C. macrocarpa Goldcrest and species); BBC Gardeners' World (gardenersworld.com, 'How to trim a conifer hedge'); RHS 'Cypress: canker' (rhs.org.uk/problems/cypress-canker); Hopes Grove Nurseries (hopesgrovenurseries.co.uk). Channel-authority heuristic applied (YouTube direct access not possible).
articlesShipped.topicGap: Cupressus macrocarpa had no existing article. It is the most commonly planted large-scale evergreen windbreak/screen conifer in CT10 clifftop gardens (Kingsgate, North Foreland, Stone Bay, Joss Bay) and a fundamentally different pruning proposition from Leylandii (which has a reduction/high-hedges angle) and Thuja (which sits in cutting/shaping technique). Canker susceptibility, the April-August window applied to macrocarpa, and the Goldcrest variety specifics are all uncovered. Fills the coastal-species category gap for the primary CT10 windbreak conifer.

articlesShipped.topicGap: Rosemary (Salvia rosmarinus) had no existing pruning article despite being one of the most common low-hedge and edging species in CT10 coastal chalk gardens. The species shares the old-wood-regeneration constraint with lavender (which has its own article) but has different cultivar characteristics, frost-hardiness profile, timing window and replacement cycle on Margate Chalk. articlesShipped.topicGap: Spiraea japonica and spring-flowering spiraea types had no existing article. The Japanese vs spring-flowering distinction is a real procedural differentiator: Japanese types flower on current-year wood and require an early-spring cut plus a post-flowering deadhead; spring types require pruning only after flowering or the display is lost. No existing article covered this. Fills a gap in the Cutting and shaping technique category for flowering informal hedge shrubs.
